s_system.text:
System. /health (version, started_at) and /health/ready (ready, dependencies[name, ready, detail]) are public; every role reaches this page from the sidebar footer. Re-checks every 30 s; calls /health when /health/ready times out. The check time shows date, time and time zone, and the copy asks for it by name.

Two panes, side by side: status and what to do on the left; what the API depends on on the right. Each scrolls on its own; the page stays still.

Current contract: a 503 from getReadiness is the generic Error (ErrorEnvelope.message only), so the build shows "The API is not ready" with every row Not reported. Each dependency has two boards: the current contract (build this) and, below it, the version where the 503 names what failed (Needs API).

On-call (owner): every failure names the platform on-call person with a Call button and links the runbook recorded in issue 66. [ON-CALL NAME] and [ON-CALL PHONE] are placeholders until the owner names them.

Dependencies as connected (DependencyReport, getDependencyStatus) is a later version (owner decision, round 2): the launch page uses the readiness check only, and the boards that draw it are marked Later version. When it ships it is for ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN, hidden for support agents. Needs API: browser-reachable DependencyReport; configured address per dependency. bucket_privacy, PostGIS and stripe_livemode are start-up gates (platform spec, fail loud on config): a failure stops the API, so the boards drawing a running API with them failed are labelled defensive.

Support agents: the left pane says what customers may notice and what to tell them; the on-call engineer is only the escalation, and replica or 503 detail stays on the admin page. A failed SMS-sender check is also a sticky banner on every admin page (customers and riders sign in with phone codes only); the email-domain check stays on this page.

s_alerts.text:
Live alerts. On open: subscribe to admin:ops and resume with after_seq = cursor_seq − 1000 (floor 0). That replays up to 1000 channel events, queue_depth frames included, not 1000 alerts, so the copy promises only "recent alerts the live connection can replay (at most the last 7 days)". Subtitles and empty states say "N recent alerts" / "No recent alerts"; "last 7 days" only when the replay started at seq 0 (cursor_seq ≤ 1000) and truncated is false; truncated means older alerts couldn't be replayed. Needs API: REST alert history, or a replay limited to alert events. Held rows wait while pointer or focus is in the list. One status region per page (next to the Live badge); countdowns are never live.

Rows are one tab stop; Enter or click opens the alert in the in-page panel (what happened, amounts, what to do). Links in About are their own tab stops. Full IDs wrap; copy is a component gap. About: Platform only when subject_type is PLATFORM or subject_id is null; CUSTOMER shows Customer and the ID, no link, for every role; any other type shows the raw type and the full ID, no link. RESTAURANT: Open this restaurant's orders (listOrdersAdmin?restaurant_id); RIDER: Open this rider's active orders (listOrdersAdmin?account_id + active states; Needs API: confirm account_id matches riders). Onboarding record is a secondary link. Support agents get the order link and the ID only: no Onboarding record link (support may read a rider or restaurant only from a case); orders open with PII masked. Unknown event types are kept with their raw type. Kind shows Platform alert plus the kind code in mono. Severity is blank for events that have none.

Queue chips: Halal certificates to review (first, no count; for support agents "Halal certificates · view only"), Failed refunds, Open disputes, Restaurant applications, Rider applications, named as in the sidebar; the count is in the accessible name. For support agents the two Review chips (Halal certificates, Restaurant applications) carry "· view only", in the visible label and the accessible name, matching the sidebar. Support agents have no rider queue (owner decision, round 2): no Rider applications chip; they open a rider’s application from its support case. Counts wait for an admin.queue_depth frame and never show 0 as a placeholder.

Needs API: halal certificate queue depth (pending checks, expiring within 30 days) in admin.queue_depth; halal alert kinds (certificate expired, issuing body status changed); admin.queue_depth snapshot on subscribe (or a REST read); history older than 7 days; acknowledge / assign (no column until then); admin.alert severity enum; admin.alert subject_type enum; alert kind and reconciliation kind lists; admin restaurant / rider profile by id; order_id on rider alerts.
Runbook (owner): linked from issue 66; high-severity rows link it. Needs content: a runbook section per alert kind. The reconciliation steps in the panel are owner-approved (round 2) and copied into the runbook (issue 66).

s_banner.text:
Banner. Sits in the system banner slot before <main>, as a labelled region. Static; role=alert only when a new high-severity alert arrives. 'Open in live alerts' on every variant opens that alert's details beside the list, focus on the panel heading. Dismiss hides it for this alert only. Support agents get their own variant: what it means for customers and what not to promise first, the raw alert message second. Needs API: severity enum.

Sessions: 401 SESSION_EXPIRED covers both the idle timeout and the absolute lifetime. Owner decision (round 2): every staff session ends after 30 minutes without activity or 12 hours after signing in, and the copy names both. Needs decision: the step-up interval; step-up copy says "a recent two-step check" until then. The session-ended alerts keep the design system's Modal: the session is gone, so nothing on the page can work.

Step-up: the staff spec names 403 REAUTH_REQUIRED; ErrorCode has no REAUTH_REQUIRED and there is no verify endpoint (Needs API). The check opens in the refund panel, in place, not over the page. The refund is not created on REAUTH_REQUIRED; after the check the client resubmits once with the original Idempotency-Key. Lost authenticator: a super admin calls the person back on the phone number on file and matches two account details and the platform on-call engineer resets it until the reset API exists (no recovery codes).

System banner slot order, top first: offline · API not ready · sign-in codes by text may not arrive (failed SMS-sender start-up check; sticky, no dismiss) · high-severity alert · What's new. Staging/local strip sits above all of them. The slot pushes content down and never covers it.

t_sessions.text: My sessions — a later version, not at launch (sign out everywhere ships on Your account)

s_sessions.text:
Later version (owner decision, round 2): My sessions is not in the launch navigation; Sign out everywhere ships on Your account. My sessions: listSessions (SessionSummary: client, device_id, ip_city, issued_at, last_used_at, is_current; Limit + Cursor, no total, so Load more) and revokeSession (ends within 10 s, platform spec). Coarse location only. Staff sessions end after 30 minutes without activity and 12 hours after signing in (owner decision). The current session isn't revoked here; Sign out in the sidebar ends it. Sign out everywhere, including here: logoutAll (POST /v1/auth/logout-all, V1, all staff roles), confirmed in the in-page panel; states: in flight, timeout (outcome unknown, safe to repeat), offline (disabled), done (204, lands on SessionSignInAgain). Needs API: confirm "family" means every session on the account. There is no sign-out-all-others; it is everything or one row at a time.

Revoke: confirmed in the in-page panel; in flight (panel and row busy) · timeout or 5xx: outcome unknown, row kept, Try again (safe to repeat) · 404: already ended, row removed · 401: your session ended, sign in again · 403: definite refusal · offline: Sign out disabled. Row Sign out is Button md (44 px). The sessions table is static: Tab goes straight to each row's Sign out (Component gap: DataTable static rows).

s_whatsnew.text:
What's new. Notes come from release-notes.json bundled with the app (#97), filtered by the viewer's role (Needs decision: a roles field per note). Console version is the web app's build, not the API version shown on System status.

The notice sits in the system banner slot above the page, below any warning banner. It never interrupts: an update that arrives while a panel with unsent input is open is queued until it closes. See what's new and the sidebar What's new (SideNav, approved) open the in-page panel; the trigger carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, not aria-haspopup. Opening the panel marks the version seen and clears the New badge. Not now stores the current version as last-seen on this device (#102), so the notice doesn't return; the New badge stays until the panel is opened.

First sign-in on a device (no last-seen version stored): only the latest release’s notes are shown (owner decision, round 2), and the notice names the current version only ("The admin console is on version 1.4.0. See what's new"), with no count of versions since you last looked. Not now stores the current version as last-seen on this device.

s_a11y.text: Every artboard root carries data-density="compact" (44 px rows, owner decision); the admin app ships light only for release 1.0 (owner decision), from the design system's tokens.css. 200% zoom boards are 720 CSS px (1440 screen); the SideNav collapses into a drawer behind Open navigation, in the AppBar's actions (component gap: AppBar has no leading slot). The drawer is Proposed component: NavDrawer (shadcn Sheet, side left; the design system Sheet only opens at inline-end): Radix Dialog traps focus inside it, Escape, Close or the overlay closes it and focus returns to Open navigation. At 720 and 320 px an in-page panel takes the whole content area, with Back to the list. Reflowed zoom boards may scroll (WCAG 1.4.10); the fit-the-viewport rule is for the desktop page. Tables keep their columns and scroll sideways in their own frame. Skip to table is rendered only when the table is.

s_sidebar.text: Shared component: AdminSidebar is used by the boards on this canvas and also lives on "HalalGoes Admin — Staff & System" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Y7wjQPGX2UAtS238ZDVhU1). The two copies are separate files: change both. Its Staff link opens that canvas.

s_split.text: Split from "HalalGoes Admin — Staff & System": https://claude.ai/artifact/Y7wjQPGX2UAtS238ZDVhU1 (staff list, account detail, invite, invitee account setup, shell and keyboard). Links to those boards open that canvas.

s_account.text: Owner decision (round 2): changePassword and logoutAll move to launch for every staff role; listSessions and revokeSession (My sessions) stay a later version. Your account is in the sidebar under Platform for every role, support agents included (they get 403 on Staff). Change password keeps this session and ends every other one. Sign out everywhere confirms in an in-page panel; in flight and outcome unknown are drawn on the Your account states board; offline works as on the My sessions boards. The contract still marks both operations a later version until it changes.

c_round2.text:
Round 2 launch contract changes this canvas needs:
• changePassword and logoutAll move to launch (Your account).
• sms_sender start-up check result readable by every admin role at launch (on /health or as an admin.alert): the SMS sender notice on System status and the sticky banner on every admin page. Readiness reports Ready when sms_sender fails, and the dependency report is host-only and a later version.
